verdict.rationale: Sill's own optional virtual display moves a streamed window onto a separate display on the Mac so it keeps updating when other windows cover it. That covers the occlusion half of the story directly. Nothing in the evidence shows the virtual display working when the Mac runs headless (no physical monitor), so the story is only partly covered. Missing for 10: evidence of headless operation, in-depth docs on configuring the virtual display, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power user, the host can create a virtual display, so a streamed window keeps rendering when covered or the machine runs headless

citations.quote: The virtual display (off by default) moves a window you stream onto a display of its own on your Mac, so it keeps updating when other windows cover it.
